assessment.nobel_worthiness: Zurita's long poetic sequences (Purgatory, Anteparadise and later books) combine a distinctive, hallucinatory and elegiac voice with a formal ambition that extends poetry into landscape-scale and public gestures. His work turns collective suffering, especially under the Chilean dictatorship, into memorial form. Few poets pursue this scope with such consistency. Its fit with the idealist direction of Nobel's will rests on the depth of the work, not on its political symbolism.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer with a clear citation scope: poetry in Spanish that carries historical catastrophe into new lyric and memorial forms. The citation should rest on the poetry itself, and the non-textual interventions should be treated as context.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre spans more than four decades, from the late 1970s onward, with sustained intensity and continued late production. Its significance across Spanish-language poetry is well established, so the timing is mature.
uncertainties: Translation: the density and sonic qualities of the Spanish are only partly carried into English and Swedish, so my assessment of the language is partly mediated.
Uncertain how well the landscape and visual interventions can be judged as literature rather than as art or performance.
I do not claim to have independently verified the full corpus or its recent volumes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Can Xue has an unmistakable voice. Her fiction breaks psychological realism and causal narrative through dream logic, allegory and estrangement. Works such as Frontier and Love in the New Millennium show formal radicalism and imaginative autonomy, and the body of work is sustained and idiosyncratic. Her place within Chinese experimental writing is distinct from that of the realist and historical mainstream.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be formally radical Chinese fiction that reworks the possibilities of narrative. Her stories, novellas and novels are all part of one consistent project.
assessment.maturity: Active since the 1980s with a large, consistent corpus that has deepened rather than repeated itself. Her reputation is secure among specialists, though the wider reception is still developing.
uncertainties: Translation: a limited share of the corpus is available in English, and difficulty of translation may affect how the prose style is perceived.
Her reception in critical discourse is uneven, and the evaluation depends partly on interpretive frameworks that vary.
Uncertain how much variation exists within a very consistent method over the full oeuvre.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adonis is a major reshaper of modern Arabic poetic language. Through myth, fragmentation and sustained engagement with the classical tradition (Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses), he opened new formal paths. His critical writing on tradition and change adds intellectual depth, and the poetry is internationally influential.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be poetic renewal of Arabic language and form, with essays on poetics as a secondary strand. His achievement as a poet and his role as a critic are both substantial but should be kept distinct.
assessment.maturity: A career of seven decades with an undisputed place in modern Arabic poetry. Timing is mature, with the open question being whether the committee considers the case long overdue or already well recognised.
uncertainties: Translation: Arabic prosody and the effect of his formal innovations are difficult to render, so judgments of language rely partly on commentary and on translated selections.
Uncertain how the late work compares with the work from the 1960s to 1980s.
Political and cultural symbolism must not substitute for literary assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cărtărescu is a visionary prose writer whose densely patterned fiction (the Blinding trilogy, Solenoid) turns memory, the body and the imagination into a metaphysical project. His voice is distinctive and his scale ambitious, and the lineage from Romantic and modernist traditions is clear. The poetry and essays reinforce the stylistic coherence.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be visionary Romanian-language prose, with poetry as a foundation. The key question is whether his originality is sufficient beyond the literary lineage he draws on.
assessment.maturity: A long career from the 1980s with major late works. The scale of Solenoid suggests continued development rather than a settled late style.
uncertainties: Translation: the lexical richness and syntax of the Romanian are difficult to render, and only part of the corpus, including the poetry, is available in languages I can reference.
Uncertain whether the sheer length of the later novels is sustained at the same level of density throughout.
I do not claim to have read these works or verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson's hybrid works (Autobiography of Red; Nox) unite classical scholarship, lyric, translation and visual form, and her voice is inventive, sharp and recognisable. Formal ambition is high, and the engagement with the ancient world gives intellectual depth. Her reworking of genre boundaries is widely seen as original.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope is poetry and hybrid forms in English, including her translations and adaptations of Greek material. Some of the work is closer to scholarship and translation than to original verse, which affects how the citation would be framed.
assessment.maturity: Active since the early 1990s with a coherent trajectory and many experiments in form. The question is whether the late work extends the achievement of the central books.
uncertainties: Uncertain how the committee weighs hybrid and book-object forms against the sustained development of a single genre.
The oeuvre is varied, so quality across the entire body of work, including performances and collaborations, is difficult to assess.
Some reception may depend on academic and classical contexts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tawada writes in Japanese and German and makes linguistic estrangement a creative principle (The Emissary; Memoirs of a Polar Bear). Her prose, poetry and drama show inventive form, wit and an unusual relation to language itself. The significance lies in a literature that crosses linguistic borders, not in thematic migration.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be bilingual writing that makes the foreignness of language a source of form. Separating the two language bodies of work is a necessary part of the evaluation.
assessment.maturity: A career since the 1980s with a stable and growing international reception. Her late work is continuing; the full measure of her achievement may still be developing.
uncertainties: Translation: much of the effect is in the play between languages, which is hard to judge through translation into Swedish or English.
Uncertain how the German-language work compares in depth with the Japanese-language work.
Her reception in the major critical traditions is less settled than some other candidates'.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Robinson's meditative prose and moral interiority (Housekeeping; Gilead) bring theology, family and American history together in a calm and distinctive voice. The language is precise and the imaginative depth considerable, and her essays add an intellectual dimension. The quality is high, though the fiction output is comparatively compact.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be contemplative English-language fiction and essays on faith and civic life. The fiction and the essays should be weighed together, but the fiction carries the claim.
assessment.maturity: Housekeeping dates from 1980 and the Gilead novels from 2004 onward, which indicates a late-flowering but sustained achievement. The body of work is smaller than that of several other candidates.
uncertainties: Uncertain whether the thematic and stylistic range is wide enough across a relatively small number of novels.
Her essays express public views that should not be allowed to influence literary assessment.
I do not claim to have verified the full bibliography.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright's large polyphonic novels (Carpentaria; The Swan Book) remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time. Her narrative scale and linguistic energy are distinctive, and her work expands what the English-language novel can hold. The formal inventiveness is central, with the political context relevant to the content but not a substitute for literary judgment.
assessment.attribution: A single credited writer; the citation scope would be English-language fiction that draws on Aboriginal storytelling and its relationship to place. Her nonfiction is a smaller strand that supports the main body of work.
assessment.maturity: Her principal novels appeared from the late 1990s onward, and the oeuvre is still developing. Sustained quality is evident, though the body of work is smaller than for many longer-established candidates.
uncertainties: Uncertain whether the novels' length and density are sustained across the whole body of work.
Cultural and linguistic contexts mean that some of the work's significance may be only partly accessible without specialist guidance.
I do not claim to have read the works or verified reception independently.
